frase_gancho.texto: High on the hill, the castle opens to the open air with intimate gardens, panoramic terraces, and a tower that once served as an observatory.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Here the castle steps out of its halls and into the open air. What this area tells is found in the hill itself. A museum wall label places the highest part of the promontory at about forty-five meters above Mexico City. It explains that from the summit one commands the whole basin. An INAH bulletin also recalls that the hill was a strategic point for military campaigns. The terraces changed with each era. Under Maximilian and Carlota, a panoramic terrace was built in front of the eastern rooms. In eighteen seventy-eight, one terrace was enlarged for the first National Astronomical Observatory. During the Porfiriato, a large stained-glass window was installed on the east terrace of the Upper Floor, which, according to the museum, is preserved to this day. In this area there is an intimate garden, a turret, a lookout, and the memory of a defense. They are four ways of understanding the history of a single place.
